newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH GOVT SETS NATIONAL ELECTRICITY GRID FIRM.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH GOVT SETS NATIONAL ELECTRICITY GRID FIRM.

text.p: The government on Thursday decided to set up a new national electricity grid company by merging the grids of state-owned Imatran Voima Oy (IVO) and big industry's Pohjolan Voima (PVO) into one firm, the government said in a statement.
By establishing this company, the government removed a major obstacle for the planned privatisation of IVO.
"The ministry of trade and industry, Imatran Voima and Pohjolan Voima have agreed to establish a new company to administer and maintain a nationwide electricity grid," it said.

IVO and PVO will each own 25 percent of shares ad 33.4 percent of votes of the new company, and the state will own 12.3 percent of shares and 16.4 percent of votes. The entire share capital would be 332.5 million markka.
The company, scheduled to start operations on April 1, 1997, will purchase the grids owned by IVO and PVO, the government said.
In 1997, Finland is likely to join the Nordic electricity bourse and the role of the nationwide grid will be to function as an efficient marketplace.

"The central operating principle of the new grid company will be to provide transfer services even-handedly and at a moderate price," the government said, adding transfer costs would be cheaper than currently. The target is to cut electricity transfer fees by 15 percent.
In September, Matti Vuoria, permanent under-secretary of state at the trade and industry ministry said the privatisation of IVO could start once the grid issue had been settled.
The government has been authorised by parliament to lower the state's 95 percent stake in IVO to below two-thirds, but to retain voting control.
